title: Should you aim for MBB, the Big Four, or both?
description: A practical way to decide where to apply: the work you want, the interview formats, your background and why applying broadly is usually wise.
hook: For most candidates the answer is both: aim for the firms whose work you actually want, and spread applications across MBB, the Big Four and other strategy firms so you have several good chances rather than one. Many candidates treat anything other than MBB as second best, which leaves a lot of strong careers on the table. The better question is which kind of work and which teams suit you, and how to prepare efficiently for all of them at once.
body:
Start with the work you want

  • Short, high-level strategy projects: MBB, the Big Four strategy arms (Monitor Deloitte, Strategy& at PwC, EY-Parthenon, KPMG's strategy group) and firms such as Oliver Wyman, Kearney and L.E.K.
  • Technology, transformation or implementation: the Big Four and Accenture have some of the largest practices, and MBB do this work too.
  • One industry you love: look for firms and teams known for it, including specialists.

Neither group is automatically better. A generalist strategy role offers variety and exposure to senior decisions; an 18-month transformation programme lets you see whether a change actually improves results. Choose based on the skills you want to build. The types of consulting explains the differences.

Think about your odds

MBB hire relatively few people from a very large pool of applicants. The Big Four hire far more, at every level. Applying across both groups gives you more interviews, and more interviews make you better at interviewing. Careers are not fixed by your first firm either: many consultants move between firms, or into industry, later on.

Know how the formats differ

MBB interviews centre on individual cases and in-depth personal experience questions, often after an online assessment such as McKinsey Solve or BCG's Casey online case. Big Four processes vary by country and role, and often include online reasoning tests, recorded video interviews, assessment centres or group exercises, as well as cases. Their strategy arms interview much more like MBB.

If you apply to both, practise working in a group as well as solo cases (how group and written cases work), and prepare for online tests and digital cases.

Comparing two options with numbers

Suppose you are weighing a generalist strategy role against a Big Four technology strategy team. Pick the criteria that matter to you, weight them, and score each option from 1 to 5. This example is illustrative; your weights will differ.

CriterionWeightStrategy roleTech strategy team
Learning and variety30%54
Fit with the work you want30%35
Location20%34
Team and mentors20%43
  • Strategy role: 0.3 × 5 + 0.3 × 3 + 0.2 × 3 + 0.2 × 4 = 1.5 + 0.9 + 0.6 + 0.8 = 3.8.
  • Tech strategy team: 0.3 × 4 + 0.3 × 5 + 0.2 × 4 + 0.2 × 3 = 1.2 + 1.5 + 0.8 + 0.6 = 4.1.

The point is not the decimal. Writing it down forces you to say what you value, and often shows that the brand you assumed you wanted is not the best fit. Use the same exercise to decide where to apply, not just which offer to take.

A sensible plan

  1. List 8 to 15 firms across groups, based on the work and city you want. The map of top firms helps.
  2. Note each firm's deadlines and formats, and confirm them on its careers page.
  3. Build the core skills once: cases, maths, chart reading and fit stories.
  4. Add firm-specific practice on top. With 60 hours of preparation, you might spend about two-thirds (40 hours) on core skills and split the rest between MBB-style practice (interviewer-led cases, deep personal stories) and Big Four formats (group exercises, video answers).
  5. Where deadlines allow, schedule earlier interviews as practice for the ones you care about most.

Strong and weak motivation answers

Applying broadly only works if each application still has a real reason behind it. Compare two answers to "Why our firm?" from someone applying to a Big Four technology strategy team.

"You are one of the biggest and most respected firms in the world."
"I want to work where strategy meets delivery. Your team advises on which systems a bank should build and then stays to implement them, and I want to see whether a recommendation actually works, not just make it."

The second could only be said to this team. More in why consulting, and why this firm.

Common mistakes

  • MBB or nothing. It leaves you with no practice and no fallback.
  • Identical applications everywhere. Recruiters notice generic motivation.
  • Separate preparation for every brand. The overlap is large. Build one strong method, then adjust.
  • Ignoring the team. At large firms, the practice you join shapes your work more than the firm's name.

Practice

Redo the comparison with "Fit with the work you want" at 20% and "Learning and variety" at 40%. Which option wins?

Show the answer

Strategy role: 0.4 × 5 + 0.2 × 3 + 0.2 × 3 + 0.2 × 4 = 2.0 + 0.6 + 0.6 + 0.8 = 4.0. Tech strategy team: 0.4 × 4 + 0.2 × 5 + 0.2 × 4 + 0.2 × 3 = 1.6 + 1.0 + 0.8 + 0.6 = 4.0. A tie. When the answer swings on one weight, that weight is the real decision, so think hard about it.

Where to go next

Start with the firm guides: McKinsey, BCG and Deloitte. Then plan your preparation with the six-week plan.
